spec.semantics: Clients send requests with magic 0x4242, command/version 0x0101, a 16-bit big-endian byte length, and an array of 16-bit big-endian integer arguments. The server responds with magic 0x4242, status/response header 0x0181, a 16-bit big-endian length (0x0004), and a 32-bit big-endian integer result. In session 3, an error status code 0x0001 is observed in the response result field alongside a negative result value, whereas successful requests show 0x0000.

observations.claim: Session 1 client request payload starts with magic 4242 and version/command 0101 followed by length and arguments.
Session 1 server response payload starts with magic 4242 and response header 0181.
Session 3 server response exhibits an error status code 0001 in the upper 16 bits of the 4-byte result field.

unknowns: The exact mathematical operation performed by the server on the input arguments to produce the result value.
The full enumeration of possible command codes and error codes beyond 0x0101 and status codes 0x0000/0x0001.

spec.semantics: The server reads a 6-byte header consisting of two magic bytes 'B' (0x42), version 0x01, command 0x01, and a 2-byte big-endian payload length. The payload length must be an even number strictly less than 0x41. The server then reads the payload as an array of 2-byte big-endian integers, sums them pairwise as 16-bit values, and returns a 10-byte response containing magic bytes 'B', 'B', version 0x01, status 0x81, a 2-byte length (0x0004), and a 4-byte big-endian sum result. Error conditions send an error response with error codes 1, 2, 3, or 4.

observations.claim: The server receives a 6-byte header to begin parsing the request.
The first two bytes of the request must be 'B' and 'B'.
The payload length is retrieved as a 2-byte big-endian integer.
The payload length must be even and less than 0x41.
The server reads the payload data based on the length.
The server processes the payload in 2-byte chunks, summing them up.
The server sends a 10-byte response back to the client.

unknowns: The exact protocol definition for error responses sent by send_error beyond their integer error codes 1, 2, 3, and 4.
